question: A 25-year-old previously healthy woman is admitted to the hospital with progressively worsening shortness of breath. She reports a mild fever. Her vital signs at the admission are as follows: blood pressure 100/70 mm Hg, heart rate 111/min, respiratory rate 20/min, and temperature 38.1℃ (100.6℉); blood saturation on room air is 90%. Examination reveals a bilateral decrease of vesicular breath sounds and rales in the lower lobes. Plain chest radiograph demonstrates bilateral opacification of the lower lobes. Despite appropriate treatment, her respiratory status worsens. The patient is transferred to the intensive care unit and put on mechanical ventilation. Adjustment of which of the following ventilator settings will only affect the patient’s oxygenation?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bilateral opacification of lower lobes on chest radiograph" -> "suggestive of pneumonia" -> "causing ventilation-perfusion mismatch" -> 80% CHAIN: "Mechanical ventilation" -> "provides respiratory support" -> "can be adjusted to optimize oxygenation" -> 85% CHAIN: "Adjustment of FiO2 on ventilator" -> "directly affects the amount of oxygen delivered to the patient" -> "improves oxygenation" -> 80%
analysis: In this scenario, the patient is presenting with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) characterized by bilateral opacification of the lower lobes on chest radiograph, decreased breath sounds, and worsening respiratory status despite treatment. The primary concern is oxygenation due to the low blood saturation. Adjusting the FiO2 (Fraction of Inspired Oxygen) and PEEP (Positive End-Expiratory Pressure) settings on the ventilator will directly impact the patient's oxygenation by influencing the amount of oxygen delivered and the pressure in the lungs to keep the alveoli open.
